document.abstract: The arrival of digital video equipment in the broadcast industry brought high expectations of increased efficiency and convenience in addition to improved picture quality. Many believed that video and audio material would be treated similarly to computer files for managing, processing, and transferring via computer networks and servers. This analogy to computer data systems–as used in office automation, for example–is too simplistic and cannot be applied directly to the demanding video and audio system architecture of a broadcast facility. Stringent requirements must be placed on broadcast A/V systems to deliver high volumes of data, in continuous streams, to a multitude of users. Realtime throughput and predictable delays are all essential for on-air applications. While many approaches are available, this paper discusses the concept and implementation of a novel peer-to-peer networking system that addresses the specific requirements of the news broadcast environment. The paper emphasizes the merit of a simple solution to manage A/V material between MPEG-2 4:2:2 MP@ML Betacam SX workstations.

authors.bio: Chris Golson has 15 years of experience at Sony Electronics. At the helm of Broadcast and Production National Sales Manage-ment, he is responsible for establishing sales strategies for key applications and/or sales channels, in collaboration with marketing applications teams and product and systems groups in the areas of broadcast and production. Prior to his current position, Golson served as vice-president for Broadcast and Production Systems Storage Marketing for eight years, where, among other accomplishments, he was key in the success of the Betacam, Betacam SP, and Digital Betacam product lines as well as the launch of the Betacam SX family of products. During his tenure at Sony, Golson has held positions as product manager for monitors and manager for marketing development. Golson has a B.A. degree from Tufts University in Massachusetts. He is a member of the Society of Broadcast Engineers and SMPTE.

authors.bio: Dave Tansek is an application and development manager, Automation and Transmission Systems, for the Business and Professional Group of Sony Electronics. He has been with Sony for 24 years and has held a variety of positions. He started out in Consumer Services and joined the Broadcast Division at its inception. Tansek worked as a field engineer until his product development activities brought him to California as a software engineer. He later became engineering manager of Switcher, DME, Editor, and Audio Products. Tansek received a B.A. degree from Wayne State University in Detroit, MI. He is a member of SMPTE.

authors.bio: Nobuaki Sato graduated from the Fukui National Polytechnic School in 1971 with a degree in electrical engineering. He then joined Sony, where he worked in the VTR design group, for six years, until he was dispatched to work as the VTR product manager with Sony sales and marketing companies abroad. Since returning to Japan, Sato has been working in the Product Planning Department for Broadcast Applications.
